newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Jordan asks Israel not to embarrass Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Jordan asks Israel not to embarrass Arafat.

text.p: Calling for resumption of the Middle East peace process, Jordan on Monday appealed to Israel not to embarrass Palestinian President Yasser Arafat by encouraging hardliners among his people.

Addressing the U.N. General Assembly, Khaled Madadha, Jordan's minister of state for foreign affairs, said the Middle East's history of missed peace opportunities should not be repeated. "Nevertheless, we are again hearing certain nervous calls and appeals advocating the revival of the obsolete security theory and the imposition of solutions by force."

Arafat, by challenging opponents of peace, should not be rewarded "by embarrassing him before his Palestinian people and putting him in an unenviable situation vis-a-vis those opponents of peace who have bet on the failure of his course and of the peace process," Madadha said.

Nor, he said, was it prudent to stipulate that Syria and Lebanon should return to the peace talks without preconditions as if previous negotiations had not taken place at all. He said it should be clear to all that dialogue rather than power politics and imposition of force was the way of the future.
"For we all have missed in the past invaluable opportunities for the achievement of peace," he said. "And here we are again about to return to that insane policy."

"So let us get back to working together in order not to kill this baby in its cradle and kill along with it our peoples' chances for a better life, which loomed on the horizon after decades of death and destruction."

Madadha also called for lifting economic sanctions against Iraq, which he said punished civilians "but did not affect their leadership." In the meantime, he said, there should be speedy implementation of a partial lifting of the embargo allowing Iraq to sell some oil in order to provide food and medicine to its people.
The so-called oil-for-food plan was delayed last month after Iraq's offensive in Kurdish territories to aid one Kurdish faction.
